why_use_this:
Reach for this package when a vāṇी program needs to run inference through a pre-built TensorRT engine on an NVIDIA GPU -- the highest-throughput, lowest-latency way to serve a trained deep-learning model on NVIDIA hardware. This package does NOT build engines from a model (that's TensorRT's own trtexec CLI tool's job, run once offline); it loads an already-built .engine file, discovers its input/output tensors by name, and runs inference asynchronously. Pair it with vani-cuda for the device-memory allocation and host<->device copies each tensor address needs.

This package targets TensorRT 10+ exclusively, with no backward compatibility for older TensorRT releases -- it binds TensorRT's current tensor-name-based execution API (setTensorAddress/enqueueV3), not the older positional-index bindings API those releases used and TensorRT 10 removed. If you're on an older TensorRT install, this will not work as written.

**Read this before using anything below -- this package carries real, unusual risk beyond the rest of the hardware-acceleration tier**: it was written from TensorRT's documented API contract, but TensorRT itself was never available to check the shim against at all in the development environment (no NVIDIA Developer account access, unlike the CUDA/HIP Toolkits which were at least apt-installable). See the README's "Hardware AND SDK-availability verification status" section.
